# LLMCSS full specification for AI agents (llms-full.txt)

## 1. What LLMCSS is

LLMCSS is a pure native CSS UI framework for AI coding agents and human developers. Every class name is listed in classes.json; classes carry no prefix.
One stylesheet ships every class and token under `@layer reset, tokens, base, components, utilities`.
Generated JSON manifests state exactly which classes, tokens, states and components exist, so an agent never has to guess.
Components, section templates and page blueprints are addressable by id.
An optional one-file runtime adds modal, drawer, dropdown, accordion, tabs, toast and command palette behavior. Everything else is CSS only.

[stats:start]
Classes: 2301 classes across 40 families, https://llmcss.io/classes.json.
Tokens: 108 --ai-* custom properties, https://llmcss.io/tokens.json.
States: 38 is-* classes, https://llmcss.io/states.json.
Components: 125, all MIT: 54 primitive, 42 application, 23 marketing, 6 ecommerce.
Motion demos: 8, in the optional addon.
Layout variants: 188 across 66 components, addressed component:variant.
Section templates: 55 (44 free wireframe, 11 themed Pro).
Page blueprints: 6 (4 free, 2 Pro).
Motion addon: 64 classes, 2.0KB gzipped, https://llmcss.io/classes.motion.json.
[stats:end]

## 2. Install

The stylesheet is the whole install for every CSS-only component. Add the runtime tag only if the page uses interactive components.

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://llmcss.io/llmcss.css" />
<script src="https://llmcss.io/llmcss.js" defer></script>
```

Pin a release with the versioned path. Versioned files are served immutable; the unversioned paths always track the latest release.

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://llmcss.io/v/0.4.0/llmcss.css" />
<script src="https://llmcss.io/v/0.4.0/llmcss.js" defer></script>
```

From npm: `npm install llmcss`, then import `llmcss/llmcss.css` and, if needed, `llmcss/llmcss.js`.

### Before you return markup

Run these before handing markup back:

- `npx llmcss validate <file>`: warns on unknown classes (errors under `--strict`) and always fails on a stray `ai-` prefix.
- `npx llmcss lint --fix <file>`: strips a stray `ai-` prefix. It cannot fix a hallucinated class.
- `npx llmcss audit <file>`: checks markup against the eleven anti-slop laws in section 11.

`validate` and `audit` both exit 1 when they find issues; `lint --fix` does not, it only rewrites and reports.

## 3. Machine-readable manifests

Generated from the CSS and the registry at build time, so they cannot drift from the shipped stylesheet.

classes.json, https://llmcss.io/classes.json: every class that exists, no prefix. If a class is not in this file, it does not exist.

[classes-json:start]
```json
{ "version": "0.4.0", "generatedAt": "2026-09-13T09:58:40.961Z",
  "note": "Every class in llmcss.css. Class names carry no namespace prefix as of 0.4.0. variants lists the prefixes that exist for the class, written as md:name: responsive (sm 640px, md 768px, lg 1024px, xl 1280px, 2xl 1536px), container-query against the nearest cq or cq-inline ancestor (cq-sm 380px, cq-md 600px, cq-lg 900px), and state (hover, focus, focus-visible, active, disabled, group-hover, dark, print, motion-reduce, first, last, odd, even). A bare cq: prefix no longer exists. Nothing outside this list exists; do not invent classes.",
  "stats": { "total": 2301, "families": { "spacing": 686, "interaction": 182, "sizing": 175, "agent-extra": 120 } },
  "classes": [ { "class": "gap-4", "family": "spacing", "file": "utilities.css", "variants": [ "2xl", "cq-lg", "cq-md", "cq-sm", "lg", "md", "sm", "xl" ] } ] }
```
[classes-json:end]

tokens.json, https://llmcss.io/tokens.json: every `--ai-*` custom property with its value per context (`light`, `dark`, each skin, `<skin>:dark`, `accent:<name>`, `focus:<preset>`). A context key is absent when that context does not override the token.

[tokens-json:start]
```json
{ "stats": { "total": 108, "componentTokens": 27 },
  "tokens": [ { "token": "--ai-accent",
    "values": { "light": "#2563eb", "dark": "#3b82f6", "obsidian": "#18181b", "obsidian:dark": "#f5f5f5", "editorial": "#8c4a27", "editorial:dark": "#c48259" } } ] }
```
[tokens-json:end]

states.json, https://llmcss.io/states.json: every `is-*` state class with the components that use it, and every `data-ai-*` attribute with allowed values and whether the author or the runtime applies it.

```json
{ "states": [ { "class": "is-open",
    "usedBy": ["accordion-item", "drawer", "dropdown", "modal", "popover"] } ],
  "attributes": [ { "attribute": "data-ai-toggle", "values": ["modal", "drawer", "dropdown", "accordion"],
    "on": "button", "appliedBy": "author", "purpose": "Runtime toggle. modal and drawer need data-ai-target." } ] }
```

registry.json, https://llmcss.io/registry.json: the component catalog. Every entry is free and MIT and carries its full `html`; `stats.pro` is 0.

[registry-json:start]
```json
{ "stats": { "total": 125, "free": 125, "pro": 0,
    "categories": { "primitive": 54, "application": 42, "marketing": 23, "ecommerce": 6 } },
  "components": [ { "id": "btn-variants", "name": "Button Variants", "description": "High-craft buttons across solid primary,...", "category": "primitive", "tier": "free", "tags": [ "button", "action" ], "html": "<div class=\"flex flex-wr..." } ] }
```
[registry-json:end]

r/{id}.json, https://llmcss.io/r/btn-variants.json: one component, the same object as its `registry.json` entry. Every component id has one.

```json
{ "id": "btn-variants", "name": "Button Variants", "description": "High-craft buttons.",
  "category": "primitive", "tier": "free", "tags": ["button", "cta"],
  "html": "<div class=\"flex flex-wrap gap-3\">...</div>" }
```

r/pro/{id}.json, https://llmcss.io/r/pro/themed-hero-obsidian.json: themed Pro markup (section template or page kit), gated by a subscription token sent as a Bearer header. On success the body has the same shape as a free entry plus an optional `css` string to link after `llmcss.css`.

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer llmcss_live_..." https://llmcss.io/r/pro/themed-hero-obsidian.json
```

templates.json, https://llmcss.io/templates.json: the wireframe section templates (themed Pro rows are locked) and the page blueprints. Counts are in section 1.

[templates-json:start]
```json
{ "stats": { "totalTemplates": 55, "freeTemplates": 44, "proTemplates": 11, "totalBlueprints": 6,
    "sections": { "header": 11, "hero": 10, "social-proof": 2, "features": 4, "comparison": 1, "pricing": 2, "faq": 5, "cta": 6, "footer": 8, "app-shell": 6 } },
  "wireframeTemplates": [ { "id": "wireframe-nav-minimal", "name": "Minimal Navigation Bar", "section": "header", "tier": "free", "tags": [ "nav" ], "placement": "Top of Page (Above Fold)", "guidance": { "placement": "...", "bestUsedFor": "...", "avoidWhen": "...", "pairsWith": [ "..." ] }, "html": "<header class=\"navbar\" r..." } ],
  "pageBlueprints": [ { "id": "saas-landing", "name": "High-Conversion SaaS Landing Page", "description": "...", "recommendedFor": "...", "sections": [ "wireframe-nav-minimal", "wireframe-hero-split" ] } ] }
```
[templates-json:end]

The MCP tools `list_classes`, `list_tokens` and `list_states` return the same data without a network fetch.

## 4. Runtime contract

### What needs the script

Load `https://llmcss.io/llmcss.js` once per page when the markup uses any of:

- `data-ai-toggle="modal|drawer|dropdown|accordion"`
- `data-ai-dismiss="modal|drawer|toast"`
- `data-ai-tab="#panel-id"`
- the custom elements `<ai-modal> <ai-drawer> <ai-dropdown> <ai-accordion> <ai-tabs> <ai-toast> <ai-command-palette>`
- `.combobox` (filtering, keyboard nav), `data-ai-step="-1|1"` (number stepper buttons), or `data-ai-password-toggle` (password visibility toggle)
- `.scrollspy-link` inside a nav, optionally with `data-ai-scrollspy-root="#selector"` to spy inside a scrolling pane instead of the page
- `.split` with an `.split-handle` (draggable split pane)

Without the script every component still renders and themes correctly; combobox, scrollspy and split markup also degrades to working, unenhanced controls. Only interaction needs JavaScript, or a native `<details class="collapse">`.

### DOM nesting rules

- Modal: the toggle carries `data-ai-target="#id"`. The target `.modal` contains an `.modal-backdrop` and an `.modal-box`. Focus moves to the box.
- Drawer: same pattern with `.drawer`, `.drawer-backdrop` and `.drawer-panel`.
- Dropdown: the toggle has `data-ai-toggle="dropdown"` and sits inside `.dropdown` next to `.dropdown-menu`. No target attribute.
- Accordion: the toggle has `data-ai-toggle="accordion"` and sits inside `.accordion-item` above `.accordion-content`.
- Tabs: `button.tab[data-ai-tab="#panel-id"]` inside `.tabs-list` inside `.tabs`; panels are `.tab-panel` with matching ids in the same `.tabs`.
- Toast: `.toast` inside `.toast-container`; a close button with `data-ai-dismiss="toast"` removes the toast node. `data-ai-toast-position="top-right|top-center|top-left|bottom-left|bottom-center"` on the container places the stack; absent means bottom-right.

### State vocabulary

[states:start]
38 `is-*` state classes exist across the library; the full list, with the classes each one applies to, is in states.json. The three most widely used: `.is-active` (21 classes, including app-header, btn, btn-ghost), `.is-open` (15 classes, including accordion-chevron, accordion-content, accordion-item), `.is-completed` (7 classes, including checklist-item, checklist-label, checklist-mark).
[states:end]

- Open state is written twice: the `open` attribute and the `.is-open` class. They are interchangeable and the runtime sets and clears both. Author either one in static markup.
- Tabs use `.is-active` on the tab and its panel, plus `aria-selected="true"` on the tab. The runtime also manages `tabindex` for roving focus.
- `aria-expanded` on a trigger is owned by the runtime. `aria-invalid="true"` on `.input`, `.textarea` or `.select` is owned by the author.

### Guarantees

For modal, drawer and command palette the runtime guarantees:

- Focus moves into the panel on open and returns to the trigger on close.
- Tab is trapped inside the topmost overlay.
- Every sibling of the overlay in `<body>` is set `inert` while it is open.
- Escape closes only the topmost overlay, then falls through to open dropdowns.
- `aria-expanded` stays in sync on every trigger pointing at the overlay.
- Arrow keys, Home and End move between tabs and activate them.
- `.drawer-no-lock` or `.modeless` opts an overlay out of the inert behavior, for a panel the user works alongside.
- `window.LLMCSS.open(el)` and `window.LLMCSS.close(el)` drive the same code path from your own script.

### Pro contract

- Pro is themed section templates and page kits. The component catalog holds none: no `registry.json` entry carries `tier: "pro"`, and `npx llmcss add` never needs a token.
- A Pro section or kit has `tier: "pro"`, `locked: true` and `html: null` in `templates.json`. Its `previewHtml` is an upsell card, not the section.
- `npx llmcss template get <pro-id>` or `npx llmcss template blueprint <pro-kit>` with no stored token prints a subscribe and login hint, then exits 1.
- After `npx llmcss login <token>` the CLI fetches `GET /r/pro/{id}.json` with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- The MCP tools `get_wireframe_template` and `get_page_blueprint` on a Pro id without a token return `{ locked: true, html: null, message }`.
- Never write Pro markup from memory. It is not in the public catalog and any guess will be wrong.

## 5. Page skeleton

Theme and skin go on `<html>`; the runtime tag goes last.

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en" data-ai-theme="light" data-ai-skin="executive">
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
    <title>Fleet console</title>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://llmcss.io/llmcss.css" />
  </head>
  <body>
    <div class="container">
      <section class="section">
        <h1 class="section-title">Fleet console</h1>
        <p class="section-lead">Every deployed agent, its current task, and the queue behind it.</p>
        <div class="grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-3 gap-6 mt-8">
          <article class="card">
            <div class="card-header">
              <h2 class="card-title">Throughput</h2>
              <p class="card-description">Requests completed in the last hour.</p>
            </div>
            <div class="card-body"><p class="kpi-value">18,402</p></div>
            <div class="card-footer">
              <button class="btn btn-primary btn-sm">Export telemetry</button>
            </div>
          </article>
        </div>
      </section>
    </div>
    <script src="https://llmcss.io/llmcss.js" defer></script>
  </body>
</html>
```

## 6. Worked examples

Every class below is in classes.json. These are body fragments; drop them inside the skeleton above.

### 6.1 Form with an error state

`aria-invalid="true"` drives the error styling. `.form-hint` is the neutral hint, `.form-error` the message.

```html
<form class="max-w-md">
  <div class="form-group">
    <label class="form-label is-required" for="workspace">Workspace name</label>
    <input class="input" id="workspace" name="workspace" type="text" value="fleet-eu-west" />
    <p class="form-hint">Lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens. Used in the workspace URL.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="form-group">
    <label class="form-label is-required" for="email">Billing email</label>
    <input class="input" id="email" name="email" type="email" value="ops@"
           aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby="email-error" />
    <p class="form-error" id="email-error">Enter a complete address, for example ops@example.com.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="form-group">
    <label class="form-label" for="region">Primary region</label>
    <select class="select" id="region" name="region">
      <option>eu-west-1</option>
      <option>us-east-1</option>
    </select>
    <p class="form-hint">Data stays in this region. Changing it later triggers a migration.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="flex gap-3 mt-6">
    <button class="btn btn-primary" type="submit">Create workspace</button>
    <button class="btn btn-ghost" type="button">Discard</button>
  </div>
</form>
```

### 6.2 Dashboard row with one dominant KPI

Law 8 in practice: `.kpi-card.is-primary` anchors the row, and the supporting numbers sit in a table rather than in three more equal tiles.

```html
<section class="section">
  <div class="page-header">
    <h2 class="section-title">Inference spend</h2>
    <p class="page-header-meta">Rolling 30 days, all projects.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="grid grid-cols-1 md:grid-cols-3 gap-4">
    <div class="kpi-card is-primary">
      <p class="kpi-label">Total spend</p>
      <p class="kpi-value">$412,860</p>
      <p class="kpi-trend is-up">+12.4% vs previous 30 days</p>
    </div>
    <div class="kpi-card">
      <p class="kpi-label">Cost per 1k requests</p>
      <p class="kpi-value">$0.94</p>
    </div>
    <div class="kpi-card">
      <p class="kpi-label">Cache hit rate</p>
      <p class="kpi-value">71.2%</p>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="table-container mt-6">
    <table class="table table-hover">
      <thead>
        <tr><th scope="col">Project</th><th scope="col">Requests</th><th scope="col">Spend</th><th scope="col">Status</th></tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr><td>atlas-router</td><td class="cell-num">4,210,883</td><td class="cell-num">$188,204</td>
            <td><span class="status-pip status-pip-success"></span> Healthy</td></tr>
        <tr><td>ingest-worker</td><td class="cell-num">2,904,117</td><td class="cell-num">$121,455</td>
            <td><span class="status-pip status-pip-warning"></span> Throttled</td></tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>
</section>
```

### 6.3 Modal with a trigger

The trigger points at the modal id. Backdrop and close button both dismiss. This example needs the runtime script.

```html
<button class="btn btn-danger" data-ai-toggle="modal" data-ai-target="#revoke-modal"
        aria-expanded="false">Revoke API key</button>

<div class="modal" id="revoke-modal">
  <div class="modal-backdrop" data-ai-dismiss="modal"></div>
  <div class="modal-box" role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby="revoke-title">
    <div class="modal-header">
      <h2 class="modal-title" id="revoke-title">Revoke API key</h2>
      <button class="modal-close" data-ai-dismiss="modal" aria-label="Close">&times;</button>
    </div>
    <div class="modal-body">
      <p>Key <code>sk_live_9f21</code> stops working immediately. Requests signed with it return 401.</p>
      <p class="text-secondary text-sm mt-2">Four services still use this key. Rotate them first.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="modal-footer">
      <button class="btn btn-outline" data-ai-dismiss="modal">Cancel</button>
      <button class="btn btn-danger">Revoke key</button>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

## 7. Tokens

Every value in `llmcss.css` is a `--ai-*` custom property. Override any of them on `:root` or on a container. Exact values per context are in tokens.json.

- Radii, exact values: `--ai-radius-none` 0, `--ai-radius-xs` 2px, `--ai-radius-sm` 3px, `--ai-radius-md` 4px, `--ai-radius-lg` 6px, `--ai-radius-xl` 8px, `--ai-radius-2xl` 10px, `--ai-radius-full` 9999px, plus `--ai-radius-base`, which skins reset.
- Surfaces: `--ai-bg`, `--ai-surface-0`, `--ai-surface-1`, `--ai-surface-2`, `--ai-surface-3`.
- Text: `--ai-text-primary`, `--ai-text-secondary`, `--ai-text-muted`, `--ai-text-inverted`.
- Borders: `--ai-border`, `--ai-border-subtle`, `--ai-border-strong`, `--ai-border-hover`.
- Action colors: `--ai-primary`, `--ai-primary-hover`, `--ai-accent`, `--ai-accent-hover`, `--ai-accent-subtle`, `--ai-accent-rgb`.
- On-color text, for text sitting on a filled action or status surface: `--ai-primary-text`, `--ai-accent-text`, `--ai-success-text`, `--ai-danger-text`. Use these instead of hard-coding white, which fails Law 7 in several dark skins.
- Status: `--ai-success`, `--ai-warning`, `--ai-danger`, `--ai-info`, each with a `-subtle` variant.
- Charts: `--ai-chart-1` through `--ai-chart-6`, color-blind safe.
- Shadows: `--ai-shadow-sm`, `--ai-shadow-md`, `--ai-shadow-lg`, `--ai-shadow-xl`, `--ai-shadow-inner`.
- Typography: `--ai-font-sans`, `--ai-font-serif`, `--ai-font-display`, `--ai-font-mono`.
- Motion: `--ai-duration-fast`, `--ai-duration-normal`, `--ai-duration-slow`, `--ai-ease-out`, `--ai-ease-in-out`, `--ai-ease-smooth`, `--ai-ease-spring`.
- Touch: `--ai-touch-min` 44px, enforced on buttons and controls under `@media (pointer: coarse)`.

Focus and tap: `--ai-focus-color` (accent at 65%), `--ai-focus-width` 2px and `--ai-focus-offset` 2px compose `--ai-focus-ring`. Presets on `<html>`: `data-ai-focus="neutral"` swaps the ring to the text color, `"thin"` is 1.5px with no offset, `"none"` removes it and leaves keyboard users without an indicator, so prefer neutral or thin. Rings render only on `:focus-visible`, never on tap or click. `--ai-tap-highlight` (transparent by default) controls the tint mobile browsers flash on tap.

Density: `data-ai-density="compact"` or `"spacious"` on `<html>` or any container rescales `--ai-space-2` through `--ai-space-8` for component padding. Absent means standard.

Per-instance tokens, set in a `style` attribute on the component itself rather than on `:root`: `--ai-card-padding` (default `--ai-space-6`), `--ai-modal-width` (default 32rem), `--ai-drawer-width` (default 26rem), `--ai-drawer-offset` (default 0px, use it to clear a fixed navbar on a top or bottom drawer), `--ai-sidebar-width` (default 16rem), `--ai-section-padding` (default `--ai-space-24`).

Dark mode activates only when you set `data-ai-theme="dark"`. LLMCSS contains no `prefers-color-scheme` query, so the OS setting does nothing by itself. To follow the OS, read the media query in your own script and set the attribute.

## 8. Skins

`data-ai-skin` on `<html>` or any container. Eight values exist.

- Full archetypes, which change surfaces, radius and type: `executive`, `fintech`, `obsidian`, `editorial`, `enterprise`. The first four have the archetype write-ups in section 12; `enterprise` is a fifth full skin without one.
- Deprecated aliases: `emerald`, `violet` and `rose` are deprecated aliases of `data-ai-accent` of the same name and will be removed in 1.0; use `data-ai-accent` instead.

`data-ai-accent` on `<html>` or any container, independent of `data-ai-skin`. Six values exist: `emerald`, `violet`, `rose`, `teal`, `steel`, `amber`. Sets `--ai-accent`, `--ai-accent-hover`, `--ai-accent-subtle`, `--ai-accent-rgb` and a contrast-checked `--ai-accent-text`. Composes with any `data-ai-skin` and outranks the skin's own accent; absent means the blue default.

## 9. Utilities

Only the classes in classes.json exist.

[families:start]
Family sizes, largest first: spacing 686, interaction 182, sizing 175, agent-extra 120, position 114, typography 108, grid 107, flex 81, marketing 73, borders 70, layout 63, effects 55, dashboard 43, extras 39, animations 33, application 32, forms-extra 31, badges 28, commerce-extra 28, navigation 24, chat 19, display 19, cards 13, drawers 13, inputs 13, base 12, buttons 12, tables 12, toasts 12, modals 11, ecommerce 10, command 9, scrollspy 9, utilities 9, themes 7, accordions 6, alerts 6, cart 6, dropdowns 6, tabs 5.
[families:end]

- Grid: `grid`, `grid-cols-1` to `grid-cols-12`, `col-span-*`, `grid-auto-fit` with `grid-min-xs|sm|md|lg`, `grid-cols-subgrid`, `grid-rows-subgrid`.
- Flex: `flex`, `flex-col`, `flex-wrap`, `items-*`, `justify-*`, `self-*`, `order-*`, `grow`, `shrink`.
- Spacing: `p-*`, `px-*`, `m-*`, `mx-*`, `gap-*` on the token scale above, plus negative margins `-m-1` to `-m-4` and logical mirrors `ps-*`, `ms-*`.
- Sizing: `w-*` and `h-*` on the same numeric scale, fractions such as `w-1/2`, plus `size-*`, `max-w-xs` to `max-w-6xl`, `max-w-prose`.
- Typography: `text-xs` to `text-7xl`, `font-light` to `font-bold`, `leading-*`, `tracking-*`, `truncate`, `line-clamp-1|2|3`, `text-balance`, `text-pretty`.
- Position, effects, interaction: `relative`, `absolute`, `sticky`, `inset-0`, `z-0` to `z-50`, `shadow-*`, `opacity-*`, `overflow-*`, `transition`, `cursor-*`, `user-select-none`, `sr-only`.

Variants are written `<variant>:<class>`, for example `md:grid-cols-2`, `cq-md:grid-cols-3`, `hover:surface-1`.

  Breakpoints    `sm:` `md:` `lg:` `xl:` `2xl:`                       viewport >= 640, 768, 1024, 1280, 1536px
  Container      `cq-sm:` `cq-md:` `cq-lg:`                            nearest `cq` or `cq-inline` ancestor >= 380, 600, 900px
  Interaction    `hover:` `focus:` `focus-visible:` `active:` `disabled:`  the element is in that state
  Group          `group-hover:`                                       an ancestor carrying `group` is hovered
  Media          `dark:` `print:` `motion-safe:` `motion-reduce:`      `data-ai-theme="dark"`, print media, motion preference
  Structural     `first:` `last:` `odd:` `even:`                       position among siblings

They are not generated for every class. Each classes.json entry lists the variants that exist for that class in its `variants` array, and nothing else resolves.

### Component variants, a different thing with the same separator

`md:grid-cols-2` is a class variant, a responsive copy of a class. `hero-split:centered` is a component variant, a different layout for the same component. Same separator, different left hand side: a class name on the left means the first, a component id means the second.

A component variant is structural. The boxes move: split versus centered, media left versus media top, sidebar versus topbar, one column versus two, dense versus comfortable. It is never a recolour, a radius change or a density change, because those are `data-ai-skin`, `data-ai-accent` and `data-ai-density` on an ancestor.

Every surface that takes a component id takes a variant reference. `npx llmcss variants <id>` says what each layout does; `npx llmcss add hero-split:centered` writes it, flattening the colon in the filename; `npx llmcss info <id>` adds a `variantRefs` list; `npx llmcss search` matches variant names. Over MCP, `get_component_markup` takes `{"id": "hero-split:centered"}` or `{"id": "hero-split", "variant": "centered"}`, and its response, like every `search_components` row, carries a `variants` array of `{id, name, description}`, so discovering the alternatives costs no extra call. A component whose registry entry has no `variants` array has exactly one layout. The counts are in the stats block at the top of this file; the full list is in registry.json and in https://llmcss.io/r/{id}.json.

### Motion addon

An opt-in second stylesheet, https://llmcss.io/llmcss-motion.css, listed in https://llmcss.io/classes.motion.json. Load it after the core sheet; nothing in llmcss.css changes, and the components the core already animates (modal, drawer, skeleton) keep working without it.

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://llmcss.io/llmcss.css" />
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://llmcss.io/llmcss-motion.css" />
```

Every class is one shot and fires because something changed: `animate-fade-in|fade-out|slide-up|slide-down|slide-left|slide-right|scale-in|scale-out|rise|sink|collapse-in|collapse-out|nudge`, tuned by the same `duration-*`, `delay-*` and `ease-*` words a transition already uses, plus `once` and `repeat-2|3`. `stagger` (with `stagger-fast|slow`) delays each child by position, capped at the twelfth child. `reveal`, `reveal-up` and `reveal-scale` are scroll-driven via `animation-timeline: view()` and degrade to plainly visible content, never hidden, wherever that is unsupported; scrolling back up replays them in reverse. `transition-discrete` and `transition-size` animate `display` and `height: auto`. Six `vt-*` classes set `view-transition-name`; the addon does not ship the document-scoped `@view-transition { navigation: auto; }` opt-in itself. There is no `repeat-infinite`, and the one looping class, `animate-sweep`, is inert unless its element sits in `.progress` or `.skeleton` or carries `is-loading`, `is-streaming` or `aria-busy`, so Law 2 cannot be broken with addon classes. Reduced motion collapses every keyframe to an instant final frame; the reveal family sits inside `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` so it never depends on that fallback.

Spacing and sizing steps: `0`, `px`, `0.5`, `1`, `1.5`, `2`, `2.5`, `3`, `3.5`, `4`, `5`, `6`, `7`, `8`, `9`, `10`, `11`, `12`, `14`, `16`, `20`, `24`, `28`, `32`, `36`, `40`, `48`, `56`, `64`, `72`, `80`, `96`.

Variable escape hatches: eleven utilities read a local variable instead of a fixed value, for the cases the scale does not cover. Set the variable inline.

```html
<div class="w-var" style="--ai-w: 37%;">Off-scale width</div>
<div class="grid grid-cols-var" style="--ai-cols: 2fr 1fr;">Asymmetric columns</div>
```

The full set: `w-var` (`--ai-w`), `h-var` (`--ai-h`), `min-w-var` (`--ai-min-w`), `max-w-var` (`--ai-max-w`), `p-var` (`--ai-p`), `m-var` (`--ai-m`), `gap-var` (`--ai-gap`), `grid-cols-var` (`--ai-cols`), `transform-var` (`--ai-transform`), `bg-var` (`--ai-bg-color`), `text-var` (`--ai-text-color`).

## 10. CLI and MCP

CLI, `npx llmcss <command>`. Binaries are `llmcss` and `llmcss-mcp`, with `cssai` and `cssai-mcp` as aliases.

```
list                      List all components, free and Pro
search <query>            Search by keyword, tag, or alias
info <id>                 Print raw component metadata, plus variantRefs. Takes <id>:<variant>
add <id>                  Write component HTML into components/<category>/. Takes <id>:<variant>
variants <id>             List a component layout variants, one line each
templates                 List the wireframe section templates
template get <id>         Print one section's HTML
template blueprints       List the full-page blueprints
template blueprint <id>   Assemble and print a full page
harness [archetype]       Print the archetypes and the anti-slop laws
audit <file>              Run the anti-slop checks against a file
validate <file>           Warn on unknown classes (--strict to fail); always flag a stray ai- prefix
lint --fix <file>         Strip a stray ai- prefix
trim <glob...>            Optional: subset llmcss.css to the classes your markup uses
init                      Write llmcss.config.json
login <token>             Store a Pro license token
help                      Print this list
```

MCP, `npx llmcss-mcp`, a stdio JSON-RPC server. `cssai_get_harness` and `cssai_slop_audit` are aliases of the two `llmcss_` tools.

```
search_components         Search the catalog by keyword, tag, category, or variant name; rows carry a variants array
get_component_markup      Return one component's HTML. Optional variant argument, or id written "parent:variant"
validate_markup           Check a snippet for unknown, hallucinated, or ai-prefixed classes
list_classes              Every class, filterable by family or variant
list_tokens               Every --ai-* token, filterable by group and context
list_states               Every is-* state class and data-ai-* attribute
llmcss_get_harness        The archetype tokens and the anti-slop laws
llmcss_slop_audit         Audit a snippet against the anti-slop laws
list_wireframe_templates  The section templates with placement guidance
get_wireframe_template    One section template's HTML and guidance
get_page_blueprint        One assembled multi-section page recipe
```

## 11. The eleven anti-slop laws

Generated from src/registry/laws.mjs. `npx llmcss audit <file>` and the MCP tool `llmcss_slop_audit` check markup against them.

[laws:start]
1. Never nest containers: Do not put a bordered container inside another bordered container. The audit walks the tag stack and flags every `.card`, `.panel` or `.kpi-card` that sits inside another `.card`, `.panel` or `.kpi-card`. Nested boxes waste screen real estate and create dizzying visual layers. Instead: Use generous whitespace (`--ai-space-6`), subtle hairline rules (`<hr class="divider">`), or distinct background shifts (`var(--ai-surface-1)`).
2. Never pulse static status pips: Never attach continuous breathing or pulsing animations to steady states like "System Normal", "Online", or "Completed". The audit flags the class tokens `animate-pulse`, `pulse`, `animate-ping`, `ping`, `breathe`, `blink` and `animate-bounce`, and any inline `animation:` value containing `pulse`, `ping`, `breathe`, `blink` or `glow`, unless the document also carries `is-streaming`. Flashing elements demand attention when nothing has changed. Instead: Render a calm, static jewel pip with `.status-pip` and `box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px color-mix(...)`. Reserve `.status-pip.is-streaming` strictly for ongoing inference or active data transmission.
3. Never use colored left-stripe borders: Do not place thick 3px to 5px colored vertical stripes on the left edge of cards, toasts, or dialogs. This 2012-era alert tell makes every element scream for attention. Instead: Use a 1px uniform architectural border (`border: 1px solid var(--ai-border)`), accompanied by a subtle 6px status jewel pip or an inline icon.
4. Never use electric purple or cyan halos and radial glows: Avoid murky dark backgrounds flooded with saturated purple-to-blue gradients or zero-offset neon drop shadows. Instead: Build depth using multi-stop physical elevation with a slight vertical offset: `box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.05), 0 8px 16px -4px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.04);`.
5. Never stamp formulaic eyebrows above headlines: Do not stamp a badge or a pill above a heading as an eyebrow, and do not repeat an uppercase monospace overline (`01 // FEATURES`, `OVERVIEW`) over every section. The audit flags a `span` or `div` carrying `.badge` or `.hero-badge` that is followed by an `h1` to `h4` within the next few lines, with `.product-badge-float` the only exemption. Repeated eyebrows become visual noise that delays reading the headline. Instead: Lead directly with a confident, well-typeset headline (`h1` or `h2`). If context is needed, fold it into the heading or the supporting sentence.
6. Never crush letter-spacing below -0.04em or justify body text: Do not apply extreme negative letter-spacing that makes characters collide, and never use `text-align: justify`, which causes distracting typographic rivers. Instead: Keep body text at tracking `0` with `line-height: 1.6`. Restrict negative tracking to large display headings (`-0.02em` to `-0.035em`).
7. Never place low-contrast gray text on colored backgrounds: Never render neutral `#71717a` gray text over an accent surface or a tinted banner. Instead: Ensure WCAG AA compliance (minimum 4.5:1 for body copy, 3:1 for large display). When the background is tinted, tint the secondary text from the same hue.
8. Never create flat, identical metric grids: Do not display 4 identical KPI cards with identical weights and icons. Instead: Establish clear hierarchy. Make the primary metric anchor dominant in size (`font-size: 2.5rem; font-weight: 700;`), with supporting secondary metrics grouped in tighter rows or tables below.
9. Never auto-scroll copy: Do not force readers to wait for auto-scrolling tickers or animated marquee loops to read supported integrations or technologies. Instead: Render a clean, static, responsive badge rail (`.badge-neutral`) or a balanced grid that users can scan at their own speed.
10. Always theme native browser surfaces: An interface is incomplete if native browser affordances revert to un-themed system defaults. Instead: Verify text selection (`::selection`), caret color (`caret-color: var(--ai-accent)`), custom scrollbars (`scrollbar-color`), link underline offset (`text-underline-offset: 0.2em`), and tabular numerals (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`).
11. Never use square grid backgrounds: Avoid covering backgrounds in repeating 20px to 40px square grid lines, dot grids, or mesh graph paper patterns built from intersecting linear-gradient declarations. This is one of the most overused, robotic hallmarks of AI-generated template kits. Instead: Lead with clean, distraction-free solid surfaces (`var(--ai-surface-0)`, `var(--ai-bg)`, `var(--ai-surface-1)`) structured with subtle 1px hairline architectural borders (`var(--ai-border)`).
12. Never paint state without announcing it: Do not mark a control as active, open, selected or pressed with a class and a colour alone. A segmented control whose current view carries only `is-active`, an accordion trigger with no `aria-expanded`, a toast that arrives outside any live region: each one looks correct and says nothing. A screen reader reads an undifferentiated list of buttons. Instead: Mirror every `is-*` state on an interactive element with the ARIA attribute that carries it: `aria-pressed` on segmented and filter buttons wrapped in a labelled `role="group"`, `aria-expanded` plus `aria-controls` on disclosure and accordion triggers, `aria-selected` on tabs, `aria-current` on the active nav link, and `role="status" aria-live="polite"` (or `role="alert"` for a failure) on anything that appears unprompted.
[laws:end]

## 12. Archetype token blocks

Pick one archetype per project rather than defaulting to generic dark SaaS styling. Setting `data-ai-skin` is enough; the blocks below are the same values, for pages that want to pin or fork them.

[archetypes:start]
Archetype A: Executive Slate, data-ai-skin="executive"
Vibe: High-density, disciplined engineering workspace, precision data tools.
Attributes: Cool slate grays, 3px architectural radius (`--ai-radius-sm`, the only skin that is not 2px), razor-sharp hairline borders, blue #2563eb accent in light mode and sky #38bdf8 in dark.
```css
[data-ai-skin="executive"] { --ai-radius-base: var(--ai-radius-sm); }
:root[data-ai-theme="light"][data-ai-skin="executive"] { --ai-bg: #f8fafc; --ai-surface-0: #ffffff; --ai-surface-1: #f1f5f9; --ai-surface-2: #e2e8f0; --ai-surface-3: #cbd5e1; --ai-text-primary: #0f172a; --ai-text-secondary: #475569; --ai-text-muted: #64748b; --ai-border: rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.1); --ai-border-subtle: rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.05); --ai-border-hover: rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.2); --ai-border-strong: rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.25); --ai-primary: #0f172a; --ai-primary-hover: #1e293b; --ai-primary-text: #ffffff; --ai-accent: #2563eb; --ai-accent-hover: #1d4ed8; --ai-accent-subtle: rgba(37, 99, 235, 0.08); --ai-accent-rgb: 37, 99, 235; }
:root[data-ai-theme="dark"][data-ai-skin="executive"] { --ai-bg: #090d16; --ai-surface-0: #0f172a; --ai-surface-1: #172033; --ai-surface-2: #1e293b; --ai-surface-3: #334155; --ai-text-primary: #f8fafc; --ai-text-secondary: #94a3b8; --ai-text-muted: #64748b; --ai-border: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.09); --ai-border-subtle: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.04); --ai-border-hover: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.18); --ai-border-strong: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.22); --ai-primary: #f8fafc; --ai-primary-hover: #ffffff; --ai-primary-text: #090d16; --ai-accent: #38bdf8; --ai-accent-text: #082f49; --ai-accent-hover: #7dd3fc; --ai-accent-subtle: rgba(56, 189, 248, 0.12); --ai-accent-rgb: 56, 189, 248; }
```

Archetype B: Fintech Titanium, data-ai-skin="fintech"
Vibe: Regulated financial intelligence, institutional security, high clarity.
Attributes: Warm stone neutrals, 2px radius (`--ai-radius-xs`), deep teal #0f766e accent in light mode and #2dd4bf in dark, generous white space. Status colors are the library defaults, not per-skin overrides.
```css
[data-ai-skin="fintech"] { --ai-radius-base: var(--ai-radius-xs); }
:root[data-ai-theme="light"][data-ai-skin="fintech"] { --ai-bg: #f8f8f6; --ai-surface-0: #ffffff; --ai-surface-1: #f2f1ee; --ai-surface-2: #e7e5e1; --ai-surface-3: #d6d3cd; --ai-text-primary: #1c1917; --ai-text-secondary: #57534e; --ai-text-muted: #78716c; --ai-border: rgba(28, 25, 23, 0.1); --ai-border-subtle: rgba(28, 25, 23, 0.05); --ai-border-hover: rgba(28, 25, 23, 0.2); --ai-border-strong: rgba(28, 25, 23, 0.25); --ai-primary: #1c1917; --ai-primary-hover: #292524; --ai-primary-text: #fbfaf8; --ai-accent: #0f766e; --ai-accent-hover: #115e59; --ai-accent-subtle: rgba(15, 118, 110, 0.09); --ai-accent-rgb: 15, 118, 110; }
:root[data-ai-theme="dark"][data-ai-skin="fintech"] { --ai-bg: #0c0a09; --ai-surface-0: #141210; --ai-surface-1: #1c1917; --ai-surface-2: #292524; --ai-surface-3: #44403c; --ai-text-primary: #fafaf9; --ai-text-secondary: #a8a29e; --ai-text-muted: #78716c; --ai-border: rgba(250, 250, 249, 0.09); --ai-border-subtle: rgba(250, 250, 249, 0.04); --ai-border-hover: rgba(250, 250, 249, 0.18); --ai-border-strong: rgba(250, 250, 249, 0.22); --ai-primary: #fafaf9; --ai-primary-hover: #ffffff; --ai-primary-text: #0c0a09; --ai-accent: #2dd4bf; --ai-accent-text: #042f2e; --ai-accent-hover: #5eead4; --ai-accent-subtle: rgba(45, 212, 191, 0.14); --ai-accent-rgb: 45, 212, 191; }
```

Archetype C: Obsidian Minimal, data-ai-skin="obsidian"
Vibe: Monochrome minimalist console, brutalist restraint, developer-first, in both light and dark.
Attributes: Alabaster #fbfbfb in light mode and pitch black #000000 in dark, monochrome near-black or near-white accents (`#18181b` light, `#f5f5f5` dark), 2px sharp radius (`--ai-radius-xs`).
```css
[data-ai-skin="obsidian"] { --ai-radius-base: var(--ai-radius-xs); }
:root[data-ai-theme="light"][data-ai-skin="obsidian"] { --ai-bg: #fbfbfb; --ai-surface-0: #ffffff; --ai-surface-1: #f4f4f5; --ai-surface-2: #e4e4e7; --ai-surface-3: #d4d4d8; --ai-text-primary: #09090b; --ai-text-secondary: #52525b; --ai-text-muted: #71717a; --ai-border: rgba(9, 9, 11, 0.08); --ai-border-subtle: rgba(9, 9, 11, 0.04); --ai-border-strong: rgba(9, 9, 11, 0.16); --ai-primary: #09090b; --ai-primary-hover: #27272a; --ai-primary-text: #ffffff; --ai-accent: #18181b; --ai-accent-hover: #09090b; }
:root[data-ai-theme="dark"][data-ai-skin="obsidian"] { --ai-bg: #000000; --ai-surface-0: #0a0a0a; --ai-surface-1: #141414; --ai-surface-2: #1e1e1e; --ai-surface-3: #2d2d2d; --ai-text-primary: #ededed; --ai-text-secondary: #9a9a9a; --ai-text-muted: #7a7a7a; --ai-border: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.12); --ai-border-subtle: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.06); --ai-border-strong: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.22); --ai-primary: #ffffff; --ai-primary-hover: #e5e5e5; --ai-primary-text: #000000; --ai-accent: #f5f5f5; --ai-accent-text: #09090b; --ai-accent-hover: #ffffff; }
```

Archetype D: Editorial Atelier, data-ai-skin="editorial"
Vibe: High-craft publication, thoughtful essay, luxury studio, timeless typography.
Attributes: Warm ivory paper substrate, terracotta #8c4a27 accent in light mode and #c48259 in dark, crisp hairline borders, 2px radius (`--ai-radius-xs`), asymmetric rhythm, zero bento card clutter. Serif display type is a page choice, not a token this skin sets.
```css
[data-ai-skin="editorial"] { --ai-radius-base: var(--ai-radius-xs); }
:root[data-ai-theme="light"][data-ai-skin="editorial"] { --ai-bg: #faf7f2; --ai-surface-0: #ffffff; --ai-surface-1: #f3efe6; --ai-surface-2: #e8e2d5; --ai-surface-3: #d9d1c0; --ai-text-primary: #26211c; --ai-text-secondary: #574f46; --ai-text-muted: #877d71; --ai-border: rgba(38, 33, 28, 0.12); --ai-border-subtle: rgba(38, 33, 28, 0.06); --ai-border-strong: rgba(38, 33, 28, 0.22); --ai-primary: #26211c; --ai-primary-hover: #3b342c; --ai-primary-text: #faf7f2; --ai-accent: #8c4a27; --ai-accent-hover: #733c1f; --ai-accent-subtle: rgba(140, 74, 39, 0.1); }
:root[data-ai-theme="dark"][data-ai-skin="editorial"] { --ai-bg: #161412; --ai-surface-0: #1d1a17; --ai-surface-1: #282420; --ai-surface-2: #38322c; --ai-surface-3: #4a433b; --ai-text-primary: #f2ede4; --ai-text-secondary: #b8aea0; --ai-text-muted: #857b6e; --ai-border: rgba(242, 237, 228, 0.1); --ai-border-strong: rgba(242, 237, 228, 0.2); --ai-primary: #f2ede4; --ai-primary-hover: #ffffff; --ai-primary-text: #161412; --ai-accent: #c48259; --ai-accent-hover: #d4956d; }
```
[archetypes:end]
